text: An oracle concerning Moab: In one night Ar of Moab is laid waste and left in ruins; in one night Kir of Moab is laid waste and left in ruins.
Bayith and Dibon have gone up to the high places to weep. Over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. Every head is shaved, every beard cut off.

versions.text: Up to the temple they go, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. Every head is shaved, every beard cut off.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew makes הַבַּיִת and דִיבֹן the subjects going up to the high places (הַבָּמוֹת) to weep. The current rendering turns Dibon — a Moabite city — into a destination alongside "the temple," which distorts the sense. Treating both as place-names (or, if "the temple" is retained, keeping Dibon as the one going up) reflects the syntax more accurately.

text: In the streets they are wrapped in sackcloth; on the rooftops and in the squares everyone wails and melts into tears.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. So the armed men of Moab cry aloud, and their souls tremble within them.
My heart cries out for Moab; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. Up the ascent of Luhith they climb, weeping as they go; on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of ruin.
For the waters of Nimrim will become a wasteland; the grass is withered, the growth is gone, nothing green is left.

versions.text: The waters of Nimrim are desolate; the grass is withered, the growth is gone, nothing green is left.
versions.explanation: יִהְיוּ is imperfect ("will become"), and the opening כִּי links this verse to the preceding lament as its ground. The present-tense "are desolate" loses both the future orientation and the connective.

text: So the wealth they have gathered, and all they have stored up, they carry away over the Ravine of the Poplars.
For the cry has gone all around the border of Moab; her wailing reaches Eglaim, her wailing reaches Beer-elim.

versions.text: Their outcry echoes along the border of Moab; their wailing reaches Eglaim, their wailing reaches Beer-elim.
versions.explanation: הִקִּיפָה means the cry has encircled or gone all around the territory, not merely echoed along its edge; the suffix on יִלְלָתָהּ is feminine singular (Moab), so "her wailing" is more precise than "their."

text: The waters of Dimon are full of blood, and still I will bring more upon Dimon: a lion against the survivors of Moab, against those who remain in the land.
